history: Quanzhou, ancient Zayton, was 'the greatest port of the East' in Song-Yuan times — Marco Polo's City of Light. In 2021, 'Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China' joined the World Heritage List with 22 sites. Kaiyuan Temple's twin pagodas, the Qingjing Mosque and Guandi Temple stand side by side — many faiths live in harmony; Nanyin music and string puppets have sung for a thousand years.
importance: World Heritage city · Emporium of Song-Yuan China
foods: Shuimen noodle paste with fried dough sticks — old Quanzhou flavor.
Crystal anhai worm jelly with garlic vinegar.
Sidan ginger-duck in a clay pot, fragrant.
Hou A-puo's pork zongzi with peanut sauce.
Four-fruit soup with agar jelly — the summer savior.
Qingming thin wraps rolled with vegetable shreds.
Minnese curried beef ribs with salty rice.
Peanut-filled soft pancakes — perfect with tea.
scenes: Thousand-year temple — the twin pagodas are Quanzhou's landmark.
Thousand-year street — the Clock Tower and red-brick houses.
China's first cross-sea stone bridge, led by Cai Xiang.
A Ming anti-pirate stone city and the Hui'an maidens.
Cizao oyster-shell houses and flower-crowned Xunpu women.
An ancestral home of Mazu belief.
